clue.text: This contains growth hormone for parts of the body

indicators.note: the word This holds the hormone abbreviation within its letters

parts.note: GH is the standard abbreviation for growth hormone

explanation.surface: A medical label saying a product contains growth hormone meant for certain body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper legs are body parts, so the plural noun fits the plural definition.

clue.text: Safe places to absorb books such as Les Misérables

indicators.note: to absorb means the safe places take the books inside them

parts.note: havens are places of safety
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Sanctuaries that take in copies of Hugo's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Misérables is read literally as 'the wretched ones', not as the novel or musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The poor and wretched of society are those lacking wealth, exactly what Hugo's title calls them.

clue.text: Babbling guru's oral meandering

indicators.note: meandering means wandering about, so these letters drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A guru's spoken teaching rambles on aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone talkative chatters on at length, which is what babbling describes.

clue.text: Recognising apparently missing millions

indicators.note: missing says the word for apparently loses the letter for millions

parts.note: seeming means apparently, as in a seeming success
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Spotting that millions of pounds seem to have gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice or identify something is to perceive it with the eyes; the -ing forms match.

clue.text: Scoffing a lot of jam's a crass backsliding

indicators.note: backsliding says the hidden letters are read backwards
a lot of says most of these words' letters, not all, are taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone mocking at length how crude a jam is, while slipping back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Scoffing a lot' as the definition, but 'a lot of' is needed to signal that only part of 'jam's a crass' is used, leaving 'Scoffing' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking, derisive remarks are scoffing, and that taunting tone is the noun sarcasm.

clue.text: Rustled up some pastry

indicators.note: rustled up means made hastily, and up here signals the letters being stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone quickly made a bit of pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: This Austrian apple dessert is a kind of pastry, so it is one example of pastry.

clue.text: Cross-talk is concerning after installing component in electronics

indicators.note: after installing means the word for concerning wraps round the other assembly

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: in places the component inside the electronics letters

parts.note: E is short for electronic, so two of them make electronics
a part is a component

explanation.surface: Discussion is about fitting a component into an electronic device.
explanation.walkthrough: Electronics is read as two electronic abbreviations, E and E, and the nesting is two deep: the part goes between them, then the whole sits inside the word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick witty exchanges between people are banter, and cross-talk is a comic routine of exactly that.

clue.text: Reference work is finally abridged

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the phrase for finally loses its final letter

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A reference book has at last been shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps is a standard reference book consulted rather than read through.

clue.text: E.g. Al and Co, and others cited in written paper

indicators.note: cited in means quoted inside, so the Latin phrase sits within the manuscript letters

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a written paper
et al is Latin for and others, used when citing authors

explanation.surface: A scholarly reference to Al and his company, with others listed in a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Al and Co look like a man and his firm; they are the chemical symbols for aluminium and cobalt.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium and cobalt are both elements of the metallic kind, so they are examples.

clue.text: Unintentionally catch bird in undergrowth striking head

indicators.note: striking head means knocking off the first letter
in puts the bird inside the undergrowth word

parts.note: cover is undergrowth that shelters game
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A bird in the bushes hits its head and is caught by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is the hunter's word for undergrowth where game hides; the rhea is a large flightless South American bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear something by chance, not meaning to listen, is what catching a conversation by accident means.

clue.text: Two friends, one rejecting maiden over a sense of taste

indicators.note: one of the two friend words rejects, or throws out, a letter

parts.note: pal and mate are both friends
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Two friends, one turning down an unmarried woman with a refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over is a cricket over with no runs scored; 'over' sits beside 'maiden' to make the cricket sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof of the mouth is also used to mean the faculty of taste, as in a discerning gourmet.

clue.text: See 28
Artist withdrawn after snorting line recklessly

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: after snorting means the shy word has taken the line in, as if inhaled

parts.note: shy means withdrawn or retiring

explanation.surface: A retiring painter behaves rashly after sniffing a line of cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without caution or thought for consequences is acting recklessly; both are adverbs.

clue.text: Son possibly saw somewhere to sit

parts.note: a saw is one example of a tool

explanation.surface: A son may have seen a place to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' reads as the past tense of see; it is the carpenter's saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A backless seat for one person is a place for sitting.

clue.text: Crooked pair of girls, Parisian one taking the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means taking away its leading letter

parts.note: fille is French for girl, the Parisian one of the pair
gal is a slang word for a girl, the other of the pair

explanation.surface: Two dishonest young women, the French one heading the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the lead' looks like being in front, but it means removing the lead letter of the French girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked as in a crooked deal means against the law, unlawful.

clue.text: An attack force, one making U-turn

parts.note: a bout is an attack, as in a bout of flu
F is the physics symbol for force
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A strike force in which one unit performs a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of direction or opinion is a turnaround, the military drill's turn to face backwards.

clue.text: Setting for aria or air to new love

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are formed afresh

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A composer arranging a song or tune for a fresh lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes 'air to', not 'aria'; the aria is in the definition, and 'or' stays as written in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song within a larger work, and a sacred choral work is one place it appears.

clue.text: Biscuits, nuts and bananas

definitions.meaning: first meaning: thin dry biscuits eaten with cheese
second meaning: things that crack nuts (nutcrackers), or simply crazy

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a shopping list of snacks; 'nuts' and 'bananas' are both slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names savoury wafers and also means mad in British slang, which both nuts and bananas also mean.

clue.text: Give credit to memory aid in case unable to get started

indicators.note: in puts the memory aid inside the shortened case
unable to get started means the word case has lost its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
a crib is a set of notes used as an aid to memory, often illicitly in exams

explanation.surface: Putting a cheat sheet in a case that will not open, then praising someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A crib is a cheat sheet or set of notes, which is why it counts as a memory aid.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a person is to credit them with it.

clue.text: Cause of spot of bother on country walk?

definitions.text: Cause of spot of bother on country walk?

indicators.note: a spot of something is a small amount, here its first letter

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk in the countryside

explanation.surface: Asking what causes a little trouble on a hike through the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the walk after the B, and the whole clue describes the answer: a thorny bush trips walkers up.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly blackberry bush snags walkers' legs, making it a typical source of trouble on a hike.

clue.text: Noise on backing tracks causing concern

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for noise is read in reverse

parts.note: a row is a din or loud noise
RY is short for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: A noise on the backing tracks of a recording is worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing tracks' looks like a music term; 'backing' reverses ROW and 'tracks' are the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or unease about something is concern, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Navy's watch out over rocky hollow

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the warning sits above the navy

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, old British schoolboy slang for look out
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval lookout watching over a cave in the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (said KAY-vee) was a schoolboy's warning that a teacher was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cave in rock is a hollow space underground, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Shot met gun shot between the legs

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shooting where a gun fired between someone's legs.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, putting the ball through an opponent's legs is a famous trick with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer's trick of playing the ball through an opponent's legs has this spice's name.

clue.text: Covering a couple of Rovers maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a floor covering of woven fabric
second meaning, cryptically: Rover is a British car make and a traditional pet dog's name, so two Rovers could be a car plus a pet

explanation.walkthrough: Rover is both a car make and a stock dog's name; read as two Rovers it gives CAR then PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor covering of woven fabric is the usual sense, and leaves can also form one.

clue.text: A sample of political wiles for constituents

indicators.note: a sample of means just a little of the word, its first letter

parts.note: arts are cunning ways or wiles

explanation.surface: A taste of political trickery offered to voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters in a constituency; here it means components.
explanation.definitionFit: The components that make up a whole are its pieces, both plural nouns.

clue.text: Amateur question-and-answer jerks and pond life

parts.note: tics are involuntary jerks of the muscles

explanation.surface: An amateur quiz host twitching, among the creatures of a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Water plants and animals are aquatic organisms, the life of ponds and lakes.

clue.text: Troy's mistake creating panic

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system used for precious metals
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: The Trojans' blunder with the wooden horse caused mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy suggests the ancient city; it is the troy weight, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme fear is terror, and panic is a sudden overwhelming fright.

clue.text: Regretted a sort of bad omen about earth

indicators.note: about places the anagram round the earth letter
a sort of means a kind of version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Someone lamented a bad omen concerning the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament or complain about something is to express regret over it; both past tense.

clue.text: Every effort made by student working with one on run

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so these letters are reshaped into the phrase

explanation.surface: A student working hard, with one more run, giving it everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave nothing unchecked is the idiom for trying every possible way, so it means maximum effort.

clue.text: Pieces of animal skin eaten by old fatty

indicators.note: eaten by means the picked letters are swallowed inside the word for old

parts.note: grey means old, as in grey-haired

indicators.note: pieces of means a bit of each word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Bits of animal hide devoured by an old, fat person.
explanation.definitionFit: Food full of oil or grease is fatty, both adjectives.
